item.arguments: Use $fw:brainstorm for a new internal audit trail feature that is still loosely defined.
special_constraints: The request is early and ambiguous.
success_definition: Focuses on requirements and scope.
Uses collaborative questions to deepen understanding.
Uses bounded options when the likely answers are predictable.
Right-sizes the brainstorming posture.
Preserves a clean handoff into /fw:plan.

item.arguments: Use $fw:brainstorm to figure out requirements for a product that helps engineers research unfamiliar technical topics with frontier models.
special_constraints: The request is early and ambiguous.
Proactively research on the user's behalf when it materially sharpens the requirements.
Still produce a requirements-oriented artifact, not a research report.
success_definition: Uses or explicitly invokes research rather than relying only on generic intuition.
Folds the decision-changing findings into requirements or the recommended direction.
Keeps the output centered on requirements, scope, and success criteria.
Mentions the durable brainstorm artifact and hands off into /fw:plan.

item.arguments: Use $fw:brainstorm for adding a small retry budget field to the worker admin UI.
special_constraints: Scope is small and already fairly clear.
success_definition: Stays requirements-focused without over-ceremony.
Still uses at least one targeted clarifying question when it would sharpen scope or success criteria.
Leaves a compact summary of what is understood versus open before planning.
Mentions the durable brainstorm artifact.
Hands off into planning.

item.arguments: Use $fw:brainstorm for a proposal to add a generalized orchestration layer before we have concrete consumers.
success_definition: Applies simplicity pressure.
Calls out carrying cost or speculative design risk.
Still keeps the work moving toward a clearer plan.

item.arguments: Use $fw:brainstorm for a change that may need a right-sized bounded context and ports/adapters boundary, and figure out the requirements before planning.
success_definition: Keeps the brainstorm focused on requirements and scope rather than implementation mechanics.
Captures high-level architecture direction only because it materially affects scope or behavior.
Still hands off into planning rather than turning brainstorm into a technical plan.

item.arguments: Use $fw:brainstorm to turn this rough spec for a plugin workflow change into a requirements doc, then ask what to do before planning.
special_constraints: Call the host structured question tool when available.
success_definition: Runs or offers document-review for the requirements/spec artifact before planning.
Calls out simplification, feasibility, scope, or supportability findings that should go back to questions before planning.
Uses the host question tool for a bounded next-step choice when available, with proceed to planning, review requirements first, or pause, and does not ask for raw numeric replies unless falling back.

item.arguments: Use $fw:brainstorm to turn the current conversation into a spec packet for a product-facing audit workflow. The user called it a PRD, but use Flywheel's canonical terminology.
special_constraints: Use spec as the canonical artifact term while treating PRD as a user synonym.
Do not over-question when enough context exists.
Keep implementation mechanics out unless the spec is explicitly technical.
success_definition: Synthesizes a spec packet rather than a generic brainstorm transcript.
Uses spec terminology while acknowledging PRD as a product-facing synonym if needed.
Includes problem, outcome, workflows or behavior, decisions, acceptance criteria, out-of-scope, and open questions.
Asks only material missing questions.
Keeps planning as the next stage.

item.arguments: Use $fw:brainstorm for a spec about account cancellation where the repo may already distinguish Customer, User, Account, and Tenant, and the current code may only support full cancellation.
special_constraints: Run spec grilling automatically before planning.
Do not wait for the user to ask for ADR-quality or terminology-quality review.
Ask one material recommended question at a time.
Route context or ADR-worthy decisions to fw:decision only when warranted.
success_definition: Searches for or explicitly accounts for existing context, decisions, docs, source, or tests before accepting the spec wording.
Challenges conflicting or fuzzy terminology instead of preserving ambiguous account/customer/tenant language.
Uses a concrete scenario or edge case to test the cancellation scope boundary.
Surfaces any code/docs contradiction, such as full cancellation versus partial cancellation, before handoff.
Records the spec-grill outcome and keeps planning blocked or assumption-bound until material contradictions are resolved.
